QF.id: VII Market Participants in Securities Markets_50

question.text: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for evaluating whether an applicant is a 'fit and proper person' for stock exchange membership?

answer.text: Absence of convictions and restraint orders

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's fit and proper person criteria include integrity, reputation and character; absence of convictions and restraint orders; competence including financial solvency and net worth; and absence of wilful defaulter categorisation. Political affiliation is not listed as a criterion. The Trap: The three distractors are all listed fit and proper criteria, so they cannot be the "NOT a criterion" answer; only political affiliation is outside the listed set. Note: Stick to the listed criteria when answering: integrity/reputation/character, absence of convictions/restraint orders, competence (including financial solvency/net worth), and absence of wilful defaulter status.
